I'm 54 years old, been farming this land for 25 years. Finished primary school — that's all the schooling I got, but I know my fields. My farm is 72 mu, me and my wife, just the two of us. My son works in Shijiazhuang, sends a bit back now and then but we don't count on it. We also do some off-farm work when the crops don't need us, but during the season the land comes first.

**Cotton — 60 mu**

Cotton is my main crop, always has been. I plant about 60 mu. This year I'm buying improved 99-1 seeds from the seed station — last year I tried saving my own seeds and the yield dropped by two bags per mu, so I learned my lesson. That's 25 yuan per mu for good seeds. I put plastic film down, about 4 jin per mu. It costs money but without it the cold spring here kills the sprouts.

For fertilizer, I do what I've always done. Before sowing I spread one bag of compound fertilizer per mu — the 15-15-15 kind, about 50 kg. That's my base. Then when the cotton starts flowering in July, I topdress with half a bag of urea, about 12 kg per mu. The extension fellow told me once I could use less, so I tried 8 kg per mu three years ago. The leaves turned yellow and the bolls were small. Lost money that year. Never again. Better to put a bit too much than too little. The compound fertilizer and urea together cost me about 90 yuan per mu.

I irrigate three times from the well. First time right after sowing to get the seeds wet under the film. Second time at flowering in July — that's the most important one, if it's dry then the bolls drop. Third time at boll filling in August. Each irrigation costs about 20-25 yuan per mu for pumping, but losing half the crop because I was too cheap to water would cost a lot more.

For pests, I spray insecticide three or four times for bollworm and aphids. Costs about 35 yuan per mu. I also spray herbicide once before the cotton comes up, about 5 yuan per mu. Weeding by hand is cheaper but with 60 mu I don't have the time.

Tillage — I hire a rotary tiller in early April, costs 15 yuan per mu, then I do furrow preparation for the cotton rows. Sowing I also hire a machine operator, about 7 yuan per mu.

Labor is my biggest headache. With 72 mu and just two of us, we hire people. My wife and I handle the sowing, fertilizer spreading, irrigation, and spraying — about 45 days between us for the cotton. But harvest? Cotton must be picked by hand. I hire about 15 pickers for most of September and early October. That's about 50 days of hired labor right there. Topping I do myself with a few helpers, about 10 more hired days. I pay about 100 yuan per day for hired hands. It adds up, but without them the cotton rots in the field.

I expect about 500 kg of seed cotton per mu if the weather is normal. Last year I got 520 kg, but you can't count on a good year.

**Sunflower — 12 mu**

The other 12 mu is on the north corner of my land, the soil is a bit sandy there. My neighbor Lao Wang planted sunflower two years ago and made decent money — about 450 jin per mu selling at 2.3 yuan per jin. So I tried it last year and it was fine. Not as much money as cotton, but it doesn't need as much work.

I use local sunflower seeds, about 30 yuan per mu. I put down 40 kg of compound fertilizer before sowing — one application, that's it. I irrigate twice, once after sowing and once when the heads are forming. Spray herbicide once and insecticide once, about 10 yuan per mu total.

My wife and I can handle the sunflower ourselves mostly — about 10 days of family labor. I hire a few people to help with the harvest, about 8 hired days.

I expect about 450 kg per mu.

**The tradeoffs**

Everything costs money. The seeds, the fertilizer, the water, the hired hands. Total cash going out this year is about 24,000 yuan. That's a big number for us. But cotton prices are around 2.8 yuan per jin now. If I get 500 kg per mu on 60 mu, that's 84,000 yuan. The sunflower should bring another 12,000 yuan or so. After all costs we have enough to live on, pay for the hired hands, and put a little aside for my son's wedding next year.

I thought about planting more sunflower because it's less work, but cotton pays better and I've been doing it for 25 years. Changing everything is risky. I'll stick with what I know.
